seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Binfield | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The sanitaryware, brassware and tile brands we fit for Binfield clients, and how our fit-only installation model works alongside your own supplier choices.

h1: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Binfield

hero.intro: We don't sell bathrooms in Binfield — we fit them. That's the fit-only model in a sentence: you choose and buy your own sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, from whichever showroom or retailer you prefer, and we install it to the standard the brand and your room both deserve. Over 30 years of fitting high-end bathrooms, certain brands turn up on our Binfield specification sheets more often than others, each with its own installation detail that matters more than most people expect before the first panel goes up.

sections.heading: The fit-only model explained
sections.body: Nothing about the fit-only model changes which brands you can bring to a Binfield installation — if anything, it widens the choice, because we're not trying to steer you toward stock we hold or a supplier we have an arrangement with. You buy from the showroom or retailer you trust, at the price you've agreed, and we check it all at survey: waste sizes, tap centres, fixing requirements and whether everything you've chosen is actually compatible with everything else, before strip-out starts rather than after a delivery is already sitting in the hallway.

sections.heading: Sanitaryware and shower toilets we fit
sections.body: Geberit's concealed cisterns, wall-hung WCs and AquaClean shower toilets are the most common sanitaryware brand we fit, and correct frame selection matters more here than with most brands, because the cistern and pan weight sits entirely on the carrier frame rather than the wall tiles. We also fit a good deal of Villeroy & Boch, bought through showrooms and retailers across Berkshire — precise ceramics and hard-wearing glaze finishes, with flush plate, pan and frame generations checked for compatibility before anything is ordered. Duravit turns up often too, usually specified alongside SensoWash shower toilet seats or a full ME by Starck suite, where the detail worth getting right early is whether the installation route is Duravit's own DuraSystem frame or a standard concealed cistern frame — the two aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded. Where a project specifies TOTO's Washlet or Neorest ranges, we plan the first fix differently depending on which one it is, since a Washlet seat adds to a conventional pan while a Neorest replaces the pan, cistern and seat as a single integrated unit.

sections.heading: Brassware and showers we fit
sections.body: hansgrohe brassware and shower systems appear on more of our specification sheets than almost any other single brand, usually paired with sanitaryware from Duravit, Villeroy & Boch or Laufen — the engineering is consistent, so performance comes down to water pressure, rough-in depth and whether the valve body was set correctly before the wall closed up. Grohe covers a wide span of the work we do in Binfield, from thermostatic shower valves and mixer taps on mid-range refits through to Rapid SL cistern frames and digital shower products on more specified projects, which is why we work through exactly what's been chosen at survey rather than treating every Grohe job the same way. Crosswater's contemporary brassware and shower systems run heavily on concealed valves and digital controls designed to disappear into the wall rather than sit proud of it, which means the work that determines performance happens during first fix, long before the finish is visible.

sections.heading: Baths, trays and tiles we fit
sections.body: Victoria + Albert's freestanding baths are cast from a volcanic limestone and resin composite rather than acrylic or steel, giving genuine weight and a cool, solid surface — a point that matters as much to how the bath gets into the room as to how it sits once installed. Where a project specifies Porcelanosa's large-format porcelain, we check the substrate and tolerance more carefully than with a smaller, more forgiving tile, because dense, rectified porcelain shows up an uneven floor or an inconsistent joint far more visibly. Matki's largely frameless shower enclosures leave very little trim to hide an inaccurate opening, so measuring, wall fixing and sequencing against tiling and the tray get planned in that order, not worked out on the day.

sections.heading: Choosing brands for Binfield's mix of properties
sections.body: Binfield has grown considerably over recent decades, but it hasn't lost its older centre entirely — period cottages, former farmhouses and other pre-war buildings sit alongside the large housing estates that now make up the bulk of the village. That mix doesn't particularly dictate which brands suit which property — a modern Geberit frame or a Matki frameless screen fits into a period cottage as readily as a new-build estate house once the wall or floor underneath has been properly checked — but it does mean the survey pays closer attention to what's structurally underneath a brand's fixing requirement in an older building than in a newer one, before any brand's product goes anywhere near the wall.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom from you?
faqs.a: No. We're fit-only — you buy your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture from whichever showroom or retailer you choose, and we install it.

faqs.q: Can you fit a bathroom with products from several different brands mixed together?
faqs.a: Yes, this is the norm. We check waste sizes, tap centres and fixing requirements across every brand involved at survey, so everything is confirmed compatible before strip-out starts.

faqs.q: Do you have a preferred brand you push clients toward?
faqs.a: No. The fit-only model means we don't hold stock or have a sales arrangement with any particular manufacturer — the brands mentioned here are simply the ones that appear most often on the specifications our Binfield clients bring to us.

faqs.q: Does it matter which frame a wall-hung toilet uses?
faqs.a: Yes, a great deal. Brands such as Geberit, Duravit and Grohe each offer their own concealed cistern frame options, and some pans aren't interchangeable between manufacturers' frames once a wall is boarded, so we confirm compatibility before anything is ordered.

faqs.q: Can you advise which brand to buy before I visit a showroom?
faqs.a: We can talk through the installation implications of a brand you're already considering, but the choice itself is yours — our role starts once you've chosen, confirming it'll fit the room and installing it properly.

faqs.q: Will you fit products bought from an online retailer rather than a showroom?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the specification is confirmed compatible at survey. We check this regardless of where a product was bought from.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Binfield brands page, a close/mid detail shot implying brand and material choice rather than a full room. Subject and action: a wall-hung basin mixer tap and a concealed cistern flush plate mounted above a floating vanity top, positioned as if mid-way through a showroom-to-site specification decision, no running water. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom vanity wall in a modern Binfield estate-house ensuite, midday, bright daylight entering from an unseen window to the side. Composition: close-to-fixture mid shot centred on the flush plate and mixer tap, vanity top and basin filling the lower third of the frame, wall tiling soft and slightly out of focus in the background. Light and materials: Calacatta marble vanity top with visible grey veining, matte black flush plate and matte black basin mixer tap, bright midday daylight raking across the marble surface at a shallow angle, creating uneven highlight and shadow across the veining rather than flat light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on any fixture; no LED lighting strips anywhere in frame; no symmetrical twin-basin staging; no uniform gold or amber colour wash; no hanging plants, florals or candles; no water shown running from the tap; matte black fixtures should show faint, believable handling marks rather than uniform showroom-new gloss.
